§15.11(i) Equations with Three Singularities

ⓘ
Keywords:
P-symbol notation, Riemann’s P-symbol, Riemann’s differential equation, singularities, solutions
A&S Ref:
15.6
Notes:
See Andrews et al. (1999, §2.3) or Olver (1997b, pp. 156–158).
Referenced by:
§31.10(i), §31.10(ii), §31.11(ii)
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/15.11.i
See also:
Annotations for §15.11 and Ch.15

The importance of (15.10.1) is that any homogeneous linear differential equation of the second order with at most three distinct singularities, all regular, in the extended plane can be transformed into (15.10.1). The most general form is given by

15.11.1 d2wdz2+(1−a1−a2z−α+1−b1−b2z−β+1−c1−c2z−γ)⁢dwdz+((α−β)⁢(α−γ)⁢a1⁢a2z−α+(β−α)⁢(β−γ)⁢b1⁢b2z−β+(γ−α)⁢(γ−β)⁢c1⁢c2z−γ)⁢w(z−α)⁢(z−β)⁢(z−γ)=0,
ⓘ
Symbols:
dfdx: derivative of f with respect to x, z: complex variable, a: real or complex parameter, b: real or complex parameter, c: real or complex parameter, α: point, β: point, γ: point and w: solution
Referenced by:
§15.11(i), §15.11(i), §15.17(v)
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/15.11.E1
Encodings:
TeX, pMML, png
See also:
Annotations for §15.11(i), §15.11 and Ch.15

with

15.11.2 a1+a2+b1+b2+c1+c2=1.
ⓘ
Symbols:
a: real or complex parameter, b: real or complex parameter and c: real or complex parameter
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/15.11.E2
Encodings:
TeX, pMML, png
See also:
Annotations for §15.11(i), §15.11 and Ch.15

Here {a1,a2}, {b1,b2}, {c1,c2} are the exponent pairs at the points α, β, γ, respectively. Cases in which there are fewer than three singularities are included automatically by allowing the choice {0,1} for exponent pairs. Also, if any of α, β, γ, is at infinity, then we take the corresponding limit in (15.11.1).

The complete set of solutions of (15.11.1) is denoted by Riemann’s P-symbol:

15.11.3 w=P⁡{αβγa1b1c1za2b2c2}.
ⓘ
Defines:
P⁡{αβγa1b1c1za2b2c2}: Riemann’s P-symbol for solutions of the generalized hypergeometric differential equation
Symbols:
z: complex variable, a: real or complex parameter, b: real or complex parameter, c: real or complex parameter, α: point, β: point, γ: point and w: solution
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/15.11.E3
Encodings:
TeX, pMML, png
See also:
Annotations for §15.11(i), §15.11 and Ch.15

In particular,

15.11.4 w=P⁡{01∞00az1−cc−a−bb}
ⓘ
Symbols:
P⁡{αβγa1b1c1za2b2c2}: Riemann’s P-symbol for solutions of the generalized hypergeometric differential equation, z: complex variable, a: real or complex parameter, b: real or complex parameter, c: real or complex parameter and w: solution
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/15.11.E4
Encodings:

denotes the set of solutions of (15.10.1).

§15.11(ii) Transformation Formulas

ⓘ
Keywords:
Riemann’s differential equation, general form, reduction to hypergeometric differential equation, solutions, transformations
A&S Ref:
15.6
Notes:
See Andrews et al. (1999, §2.3) or Olver (1997b, pp. 156–158).
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/15.11.ii
See also:
Annotations for §15.11 and Ch.15

A conformal mapping of the extended complex plane onto itself has the form

15.11.5 t=(κ⁢z+λ)/(μ⁢z+ν),
ⓘ
Symbols:
z: complex variable, t: mapping, κ: constant, λ: constant, μ: constant and ν: constant
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/15.11.E5
Encodings:
TeX, pMML, png
See also:
Annotations for §15.11(ii), §15.11 and Ch.15

where κ, λ, μ, ν are real or complex constants such that κ⁢ν−λ⁢μ=1. These constants can be chosen to map any two sets of three distinct points {α,β,γ} and {α~,β~,γ~} onto each other. Symbolically:

15.11.6 P⁡{αβγa1b1c1za2b2c2}=P⁡{α~β~γ~a1b1c1ta2b2c2}.
ⓘ
Symbols:
P⁡{αβγa1b1c1za2b2c2}: Riemann’s P-symbol for solutions of the generalized hypergeometric differential equation, z: complex variable, a: real or complex parameter, b: real or complex parameter, c: real or complex parameter, α: point, β: point, γ: point and t: mapping
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/15.11.E6
Encodings:
TeX, pMML, png
See also:
Annotations for §15.11(ii), §15.11 and Ch.15

The reduction of a general homogeneous linear differential equation of the second order with at most three regular singularities to the hypergeometric differential equation is given by

15.11.7 P⁡{αβγa1b1c1za2b2c2}=(z−αz−γ)a1⁢(z−βz−γ)b1⁢P⁡{01∞00a1+b1+c1(z−α)⁢(β−γ)(z−γ)⁢(β−α)a2−a1b2−b1a1+b1+c2}.
ⓘ
Symbols:
P⁡{αβγa1b1c1za2b2c2}: Riemann’s P-symbol for solutions of the generalized hypergeometric differential equation, z: complex variable, a: real or complex parameter, b: real or complex parameter, c: real or complex parameter, α: point, β: point and γ: point
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/15.11.E7
Encodings:
TeX, pMML, png
See also:
Annotations for §15.11(ii), §15.11 and Ch.15

We also have

15.11.8 zλ⁢(1−z)μ⁢P⁡{01∞a1b1c1za2b2c2}=P⁡{01∞a1+λb1+μc1−λ−μza2+λb2+μc2−λ−μ},
ⓘ
Symbols:
P⁡{αβγa1b1c1za2b2c2}: Riemann’s P-symbol for solutions of the generalized hypergeometric differential equation, z: complex variable, a: real or complex parameter, b: real or complex parameter, c: real or complex parameter, λ: constant and μ: constant
Permalink:
